speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your recent myocardial infarction and the combination of umbilical pain and bloody stools, I need to rule out acute mesenteric ischemia. Have you noticed any specific food triggers that worsen the pain, or does it occur at rest regardless? Also, when was your last bowel movement?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia. The sudden onset of severe periumbilical pain disproportionate to physical exam findings, combined with bloody stools and a recent history of myocardial infarction, is highly suggestive of bowel ischemia due to thromboembolism.
